label: copy-phase input k (fed-back k, past the first copied token)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase when the fed-back input token is k (in_tok k carries all activation mass). It never fires in the original phase, on the delimiter step, or on any other input token, including k typed during the original phase. It essentially never fires when k is the first fed-back token (recall_idx 1, input = orig(0)): the rate there is 0.5% and the mass is tiny. It fires on 100% of copy-phase k inputs from recall_idx >= 2 on. Magnitude grows with position in the copy phase. Examples: k fed back at copy position 2 is about 0.45 of max, while the top activations (about 1.0) are k late in the copy of long sequences. The token being output and earlier context have no visible effect.

issues: No refutation found. Test scores reproduce: precision 1.0, recall 0.970, F1 0.985, mass recall 0.999. Without recall_idx>=2 the test F1 is 0.914 (P 0.84, R 1.00), which matches the claim.

Every miss on test (2275 steps, 0.1% of mass) is a fed-back k at recall_idx 1 (first copied token) with activation of about 0.01-0.06 of max. That is the low-rate tail the explanation already describes, not a new class. There were zero false positives.

Dev profile: 100% of the mass is in the copy phase. in_tok k carries 1.000 of the mass, with 1 stray activation on h. There are no activations in the original or delimiter phases. The recall_idx 1 rate is 0.005 and its mass 0.001, both as claimed.

The magnitude claim fits the examples: at copy position 2 the feature reaches about 0.43-0.49 of max, then rises with recall_idx to about 0.98-1.0 near position 7. Minor nuance: the second k of a repeated 'k k' fed back is a bit lower (0.88-0.93) than the first. This is small and doesn't change the label.
out_tok, prev_tok and next_out all show flat lift. This supports 'output token and context show no visible effect'.
